source_title: Rajdeep Sardesai on prostate cancer diagnosis, surgery and life after recovery - India Today - India Today
source_excerpt:
Rajdeep Sardesai had planned a summer trip to England to watch India play cricket at Lord's. Instead, a cancer diagnosis changed everything. At Day 2 of the India Today Health Wealth Conclave 2026, the veteran journalist opened up about his prostate cancer journey during the session 'Humne Cancer Ko Haraya', alongside his treating doctor, Dr Anshuman Agarwal, Senior Urologist at Indraprastha Apollo Hospital. Sardesai recalled his first reaction to the diagnosis: "Why me?" He revealed that the cancer was detected during investigations before a planned hernia operation. An elevated PSA level led to further tests and a targeted biopsy. After undergoing surgery, Sardesai is now in remission and continues regular follow-ups. He credited his family, friends and doctors for supporting his recovery. His message to others was simple: do not take life for granted, speak openly about cancer and treasure the people who stand by you. Read More

'IDBI Bank is already a private bank from FY19': Soumya Kanti Ghosh
In an exclusive interview, Soumya Kanti Ghosh, Group Chief Economic Advisor of SBI and part-time member of the EAC-PM, addressed the ongoing political debate over the IDBI Bank stake sale. He clarified that IDBI Bank is already classified as a private lender by the RBI since FY19, noting that the government and LIC will retain a 34% stake post-offload. Ghosh explained that after suffering accumulated losses of 45,000 crore rupees between FY16 and FY20, a 50,000 crore rupee capital infusion helped bring IDBI's gross NPA down from 31% to under 2%, generating 35,000 crore rupees in cumulative profits over five years. Defending the strength of public sector lenders, Ghosh emphasized: 'The banking system today is actually in the best of health after all the efforts which has been unveiled in the last decade or so.' Declining to discuss corporate governance issues regarding Tata Group clients, he maintained that India possesses a robust regulatory governance culture monitored by SEBI.
IDBI Bank Sale: '81 Rupees Is Certainly A Very, Very Low Price', Says SC Garg
A debate on the privatization of IDBI Bank focuses on the valuation and bidding process surrounding the stake sale to Fairfax Holdings. Former Finance and Economic Affairs Secretary Subhash Chandra Garg argues that the bank has turned around significantly, making the sale price of ₹81 per share a throwaway valuation compared to its true worth and free reserves. Garg questions why the reserve price was lowered and contends that the divestment has turned into an uncompetitive one-horse race. In response, political analyst Rajat Sethi defends the government's disinvestment process, stating that taxpayer and LIC funds were used to resurrect the ailing bank. Sethi argues that market forces and independent institutions determined the valuation, asserting that criticism without hard evidence or alternate bids is unwarranted.
IDBI Bank Divestment Sparks Clash: Rahul Gandhi Alleges Fraud, FM Hits Back
A major political confrontation has erupted between Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman over the proposed privatization of IDBI Bank. Rahul Gandhi accused the government of fraud in the disinvestment process, alleging undervaluation and questioning the sale of an institution built with public money. Hitting back, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman cited bad loans and politically influenced lending under past Congress regimes, blaming them for weakening the bank before the NDA government revived it. The Finance Ministry also rejected allegations of wrongdoing, clarifying that the reserve price remained unchanged while the revised process increased the discovered bid price by 3,917 crore rupees.
UP Politics: 'Amit Shah's arrival in Lucknow admission to Yogi failure', says SP
A political debate erupted over Uttar Pradesh governance and electoral leadership between Samajwadi Party spokesperson Pradeep Bharti and Bharatiya Janata Party national spokesperson Charu Pragya. The discussion focused on Union Home Minister Amit Shah's visit to Lucknow and ongoing political speculation following recent election outcomes. Pradeep Bharti asserted that 'Amit Shah's arrival in Lucknow itself an admission to the Yogi government's failure' and questioned the Bharatiya Janata Party's confidence in Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. In response, Charu Pragya defended the ruling party's democratic credentials and contested claims regarding internal rift, challenging Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav to contest from Ayodhya. Bharti countered by arguing that democratic governance is not merely about electoral victories but about institutional integrity and protecting dissent.
